question: do the arms solve the same scenes, or the same number of scenes?

perfect_splits.why_conditional: a scene can only split perfectly if its total solves across both arms is exactly the number of seeds per arm. A scene every run solved cannot split under any shuffle, so the unconditional count -- 100 scenes x 2/C(6,3) = 10.0 -- overstates the null by counting scenes that were never at risk

permutation_test.statistic: mean absolute per-scene disagreement in solve count
permutation_test.null: shaping changes nothing about which scenes are solvable, so a scene's outcomes are exchangeable between arms. Shuffled within each scene, which conditions on that scene's difficulty
permutation_test.two_sided: the statistic is absolute, so this asks whether the arms solve different scenes -- not which arm is better, which the rates answer

why_not_per_seed_mcnemar: run per seed, McNemar asks whether one arm won that draw and correctly answers no on a 9-against-9 split. It cannot see whether the arms differ on the *same* scenes across seeds, because it discards the scene identities when it reduces to two counts
